intro: Hi! In this lesson you learn there is and there are, the English way to say 'ada'. You'll describe a room or a place, ask what is there (Is there an ATM near here?) and use some and any. Warm-up: what is in your room right now?
teachingNotes: Indonesian 'ada' becomes there is / there are. The biggest error is using have for 'ada': *'In my room have a bed'* → **There is a bed in my room.** Pattern: there is/are + thing + place. 'My room has a bed' is also correct English, but practise there is/are here. Two beginner confusions to address: learners know 'there' = 'di sana', so say clearly that in 'there is/are' it has no meaning of its own; and 'have' = 'punya' (an owner), which is why it can't replace 'ada'.

is or are depends on the noun after it: one thing (a/an) → there is (short: there's); two or more → there are. Common error: *'There is two chairs'* → There are two chairs. Don't teach a short form for there are ('there're'). If the learner asks about lists, the first noun usually decides (There is a bed and two chairs), but don't drill it. Watch plurals without -s: people, children → there are.
Negatives: there isn't a … (one thing), there aren't any … (two or more). Accept 'there is no / there are no' as correct, but teach isn't / aren't first.

Questions: put is/are first: Is there a …? Are there any …? Short answers use there: Yes, there is. / No, there isn't. Yes, there are. / No, there aren't. Common errors: *'Yes, it is'*, *'Yes, have'*, *'Is there two toilets?'*. Why not 'Yes, it is': 'it' refers to a specific thing already known; 'Is there…?' asks whether something exists, so the answer keeps 'there'. 'lift' (British) = 'elevator' (American); Indonesian uses 'lift' too.

some/any only with plural countable nouns here: some in positive sentences (There are some shops), any in negatives and questions. Common error: *'Are there some shops near here?'* → Are there any shops near here? Don't use some/any with one thing (There is a chair, not 'some chair').

Limits: only the present. Don't teach there was/were, there will be, uncountable nouns with some/any, How much / How many (next lesson: a1-countable-some-any) or place prepositions like next to, under, behind, between (lesson a1-prepositions). Keep places to 'in …' and 'near …' (near here, near the station).

keyPoints.title: There is / there are = ada
keyPoints.explanation: Use there is (there's) for one thing and there are for two or more, then say the place: There is a bed in my room. 'There' here doesn't mean 'di sana'; there is/are together = ada. Negatives: there isn't a …, there aren't any …. Don't use have for 'ada': have = punya.

examples.en: There is a bed in my room.
There are two bathrooms in our house.
examples.id: Ada dua kamar mandi di rumah kami.

examples.en: There isn't a TV in my bedroom.
examples.id: Tidak ada TV di kamar tidurku.

id.title: There is / there are = ada
id.explanation: Pakai there is (there's) untuk satu benda dan there are untuk dua atau lebih, lalu sebutkan tempatnya: There is a bed in my room. 'There' di sini bukan berarti 'di sana'; there is/are bersama-sama = ada. Kalimat negatif: there isn't a …, there aren't any …. Jangan pakai have untuk 'ada': have = punya.

keyPoints.title: Is there …? / Are there …?
keyPoints.explanation: Put is or are first: Is there a …? (one thing), Are there …? (two or more). Short answers use there: Yes, there is. / No, there isn't. Yes, there are. / No, there aren't.

examples.en: Is there an ATM near here? — Yes, there is.
examples.id: Ada ATM di dekat sini? — Ya, ada.

examples.en: Is there a fridge in the room? — No, there isn't.
examples.id: Ada kulkas di kamarnya? — Tidak ada.

examples.en: Are there two beds in the room? — Yes, there are.
examples.id: Ada dua tempat tidur di kamarnya? — Ya, ada.

id.title: Is there …? / Are there …?
id.explanation: Taruh is atau are di depan: Is there a …? (satu benda), Are there …? (dua atau lebih). Jawaban singkat memakai there: Yes, there is. / No, there isn't. Yes, there are. / No, there aren't.

keyPoints.title: some and any
keyPoints.explanation: With two or more things, use some in positive sentences (= beberapa) and any in negatives and questions: There are some shops. There aren't any shops. Are there any shops near here?

examples.en: There are some nice beaches in Lombok.
examples.id: Ada beberapa pantai yang bagus di Lombok.

examples.en: There aren't any shops in my village.
examples.id: Tidak ada toko sama sekali di desaku.

examples.en: Are there any shops near here?

id.title: some dan any
id.explanation: Untuk dua benda atau lebih, pakai some di kalimat positif (= beberapa) dan any di kalimat negatif dan pertanyaan: There are some shops. There aren't any shops. Are there any shops near here?

blocks.text: Indonesian says *ada* when something is in a place. English says **there is** for **one** thing and **there are** for **two or more**. Then say the place: **There is a bed in my room.** **There are two windows in the kitchen.** You know *there* = *di sana*, but here it doesn't mean that: **there is / there are** is one fixed group of words that means *ada*. In speaking, *there is* is often **there's**. *There are* has no short form in writing.

id.text: Bahasa Indonesia memakai *ada* untuk sesuatu yang ada di suatu tempat. Bahasa Inggris memakai **there is** untuk **satu** benda dan **there are** untuk **dua atau lebih**. Lalu sebutkan tempatnya: **There is a bed in my room.** **There are two windows in the kitchen.** Kamu tahu *there* = *di sana*, tapi di sini artinya bukan itu: **there is / there are** adalah satu rangkaian kata tetap yang artinya *ada*. Saat bicara, *there is* sering disingkat **there's**. *There are* tidak punya bentuk pendek dalam tulisan.

rows.en: There is a bed in my room.
There's a big TV in the living room.
rows.id: Ada TV besar di ruang tamu.

rows.en: There are two bathrooms in our house.
rows.id: Ada dua kamar mandi di rumah kami.

rows.en: There are 30 students in my class.

blocks.text: Don't use **have** for *ada*: 'In my room have a bed' is wrong. Say **There is a bed in my room.** And look at the **noun** (the thing): 'There is two chairs' is wrong, because two chairs = **are**: **There are two chairs.** Careful with **people** and **children**: no -s, but they mean more than one, so they take **are** too.

id.text: Jangan pakai **have** untuk *ada*: 'In my room have a bed' salah. Katakan **There is a bed in my room.** Dan lihat **kata bendanya** (bendanya): 'There is two chairs' salah, karena two chairs = **are**: **There are two chairs.** Hati-hati dengan **people** dan **children**: tanpa -s, tapi artinya lebih dari satu, jadi juga memakai **are**.

blocks.prompt: Your hotel room in Bali is big. Complete: There ___ two beds in the room.
blocks.explain: Two beds = two or more, so there are. 'Have' means punya (owns), so it's not used for 'ada'.

id.explain: Two beds = dua atau lebih, jadi there are. 'Have' artinya punya, jadi tidak dipakai untuk 'ada'.
id.prompt: Kamar hotelmu di Bali besar. Lengkapi: There ___ two beds in the room.

material.title: Ada or punya: there is or have?

blocks.text:
In everyday Indonesian, *ada* and *punya* sometimes mix (*Saya ada mobil*). In English they are two different ideas:
- **have / has** = *punya*. You need an **owner** first: **I have** a car. **Budi has** a motorbike.
- **there is / there are** = *ada*. Something is in a place; nobody owns it: **There is** a mosque near here.

'In my room have a bed' has no owner in front of *have*, so it doesn't work. When you want to say *ada … di …*, start with **There is / There are**.

id.text:
Dalam bahasa Indonesia sehari-hari, *ada* dan *punya* kadang tercampur (*Saya ada mobil*). Dalam bahasa Inggris, keduanya berbeda:
- **have / has** = *punya*. Harus ada **pemilik** di depannya: **I have** a car. **Budi has** a motorbike.
- **there is / there are** = *ada*. Sesuatu berada di suatu tempat; tidak ada pemiliknya: **There is** a mosque near here.

'In my room have a bed' tidak punya pemilik di depan *have*, jadi salah. Kalau kamu mau bilang *ada … di …*, mulai dengan **There is / There are**.

rows.en: There is a fan in the room.
rows.id: Ada kipas angin di kamar itu.

rows.en: There are two cats in the garden.

blocks.text: Easy test: can you say *punya* in Indonesian? Use **have**. Is it *ada … di* (something in a place)? Use **there is / there are**. And remember, *there* here doesn't mean *di sana*.

id.text: Tes gampang: bisa diganti *punya* dalam bahasa Indonesia? Pakai **have**. Kalau *ada … di* (sesuatu di suatu tempat)? Pakai **there is / there are**. Dan ingat, *there* di sini tidak berarti *di sana*.

blocks.prompt: Ada masjid di dekat sini. → Which is correct?
options: There is a mosque near here.
It is a mosque near here.
blocks.explain: Ada + a place = there is: There is a mosque near here. Have means punya and needs an owner, and 'It is a mosque' means 'Itu masjid'.

id.explain: Ada + tempat = there is: There is a mosque near here. Have artinya punya dan butuh pemilik, dan 'It is a mosque' artinya 'Itu masjid'.
id.prompt: Ada masjid di dekat sini. → Mana yang benar?

id.title: Ada atau punya: there is atau have?

blocks.text: For *tidak ada*, add **not**: **there isn't a** + one thing, **there aren't any** + two or more. Long forms: *there is not*, *there are not*. (More about **any** in the last part.)

id.text: Untuk *tidak ada*, tambahkan **not**: **there isn't a** + satu benda, **there aren't any** + dua atau lebih. Bentuk panjangnya: *there is not*, *there are not*. (Penjelasan tentang **any** ada di bagian terakhir.)

rows.en: There isn't a TV in my bedroom.
rows.id: Tidak ada TV di kamar tidurku.

rows.en: There isn't an ATM in my village.
There aren't any shops in my village.
rows.id: Tidak ada toko sama sekali di desaku.

blocks.text: Word note: a **lift** (British English) is an **elevator** in American English. Indonesian says *lift* too. And you will also hear **There's no …** for *tidak ada*: it means the same as *There isn't a …*.

id.text: Catatan kata: **lift** (bahasa Inggris Britania) adalah **elevator** dalam bahasa Inggris Amerika. Bahasa Indonesia juga bilang *lift*. Kamu juga akan mendengar **There's no …** untuk *tidak ada*: artinya sama dengan *There isn't a …*.

blocks.prompt: Rina's kos room has no TV. Complete: There ___ a TV in her room.
blocks.explain: A TV = one thing, so there isn't. 'Don't have' is the have mistake again.

id.explain: A TV = satu benda, jadi there isn't. 'Don't have' adalah kesalahan have tadi.
id.prompt: Kamar kos Rina tidak ada TV-nya. Lengkapi: There ___ a TV in her room.

blocks.text: To ask, put **is** or **are** first: **Is there a …?** for one thing, **Are there …?** for two or more. The short answer uses **there**: **Yes, there is. / No, there isn't.** **Yes, there are. / No, there aren't.** Very useful when you travel!

id.text: Untuk bertanya, taruh **is** atau **are** di depan: **Is there a …?** untuk satu benda, **Are there …?** untuk dua atau lebih. Jawaban singkatnya memakai **there**: **Yes, there is. / No, there isn't.** **Yes, there are. / No, there aren't.** Sangat berguna saat kamu bepergian!

rows.en: Is there an ATM near here? — Yes, there is.
rows.id: Ada ATM di dekat sini? — Ya, ada.

rows.en: Is there a fridge in the room? — No, there isn't.
rows.id: Ada kulkas di kamarnya? — Tidak ada.

rows.en: Are there two beds in the room? — Yes, there are.
rows.id: Ada dua tempat tidur di kamarnya? — Ya, ada.

blocks.text: Answer with **there**, not *it* or *have*: **Yes, there is**, not 'Yes, it is' or 'Yes, have'. Why? *It* points to one thing you both already know (*Is it your bag? — Yes, it is.*). *Is there …?* asks whether something exists, so the answer repeats **there**. And match the noun: 'Is there two toilets?' is wrong; say **Are there two toilets?**

id.text: Jawab dengan **there**, bukan *it* atau *have*: **Yes, there is**, bukan 'Yes, it is' atau 'Yes, have'. Kenapa? *It* menunjuk satu benda yang sudah sama-sama kalian tahu (*Is it your bag? — Yes, it is.*). *Is there …?* menanyakan apakah sesuatu ada, jadi jawabannya mengulang **there**. Dan sesuaikan dengan kata bendanya: 'Is there two toilets?' salah; katakan **Are there two toilets?**

blocks.prompt: You need medicine. Which question is correct?
options: Is there a pharmacy near here?
Are there a pharmacy near here?
blocks.explain: A pharmacy = one thing, so Is there …? Don't use have for 'ada'.

id.explain: A pharmacy = satu benda, jadi Is there …? Jangan pakai have untuk 'ada'.
id.prompt: Kamu butuh obat. Pertanyaan mana yang benar?

blocks.text: With two or more things, use **some** in positive sentences (= *beberapa*): **There are some shops near the hotel.** Use **any** in negatives (sentences with *not*) and questions: **There aren't any shops.** **Are there any shops near here?** **Any** has no exact Indonesian word: in a question you usually don't translate it (*Ada toko di dekat sini?*), and in a negative it's like *sama sekali*. With one thing, use **a/an**: *There is a shop*, not 'there is some shop'.

id.text: Untuk dua benda atau lebih, pakai **some** dalam kalimat positif (= *beberapa*): **There are some shops near the hotel.** Pakai **any** dalam kalimat negatif (kalimat dengan *not*) dan pertanyaan: **There aren't any shops.** **Are there any shops near here?** **Any** tidak punya terjemahan yang pas: dalam pertanyaan biasanya tidak diterjemahkan (*Ada toko di dekat sini?*), dan dalam kalimat negatif mirip *sama sekali*. Untuk satu benda, pakai **a/an**: *There is a shop*, bukan 'there is some shop'.

rows.en: There are some nice beaches in Lombok.
rows.id: Ada beberapa pantai yang bagus di Lombok.

rows.en: There aren't any trains to Bali.
Are there any good warungs near here?
rows.id: Ada warung yang enak di dekat sini?

blocks.text: A very common mistake: 'Are there some shops near here?' In questions, use **any**: **Are there any shops near here?**

id.text: Kesalahan yang sangat umum: 'Are there some shops near here?' Dalam pertanyaan, pakai **any**: **Are there any shops near here?**

blocks.prompt: Complete: There are ___ students in the library.
blocks.explain: It's a positive sentence (no not, not a question) with a plural noun (students = more than one), so some. Any is for negatives and questions, and a is only for one thing.

id.explain: Ini kalimat positif (tanpa not, bukan pertanyaan) dengan kata benda jamak (students = lebih dari satu), jadi some. Any untuk kalimat negatif dan pertanyaan, dan a hanya untuk satu benda.
id.prompt: Lengkapi: There are ___ students in the library.
